scope_basis: Additional financing for a digital identification project.
title: World Bank — Togo WURI digital-ID additional financing, 2026
description: "Togo and the World Bank Group signed five financing agreements worth a combined $429 million, or about 257.4 billion CFA francs, in Lomé on Thursday, July 16, 2026." "Under the 'Unite' pillar, the West Africa Unique Identification for Regional Integration and Inclusion Project, known as WURI, will receive an additional $20 million to expand access to secure identification." The other agreements — PRIME-GAS ($40m) and WA-REMP ($100m) energy, COSO social cohesion ($69m) and PASLT logistics ($200m) — fall outside data governance / digital transformation.

Une partie de cet engagement soutiendra la transformation numérique de l'administration togolaise et renforcera la sécurité des infrastructures numériques, notamment à travers le programme TogoCyber+." scope_basis: Research support to a government data lab for data-science and artificial-intelligence capacity.
title: Google.org — Togo Data Lab expansion, 2025
description:
"The Government of Togo and the Center for Effective Global Action (CEGA) at the University of California, Berkeley have announced a new partnership with Google.org that will sustain Togo's ongoing efforts to use data science and artificial intelligence to advance inclusive development and encourage evidence-informed public decision-making."

"Google.org's $2 million research support will charge the Togo Data Lab (TDL) initiative—a collaboration between CEGA and Togo's Ministry of Public Service Efficiency and Digital Transformation (MESPTN)—to support the University of Lomé and the University of Kara in developing interdisciplinary data science curricula, establishing dedicated research hubs, and channeling data science talent to pressing development challenges in Togo. These centers will provide faculty and students with access to high performance computer clusters, training on computational tools and approaches, and opportunities to apply them through real-world projects sourced from partner priorities."

"A new Data Ambassadors Program will train 27 data specialists to strengthen data governance and analytical capacity in all of Togo's government ministries."

"In its first two years, the initiative is expected to train more than 100 students and 70 government data scientists, create new university-level courses, and support over 20 public institutions in integrating data science into their daily operations."

title: Axian Togo / Togocom Telecom Expansion Loan
description: IFC provided a senior loan of up to €50 million from its own account (A-loan) to Togocom, Togo's privatised incumbent telecoms operator and a subsidiary of Axian Group, to support modernisation and expansion of its mobile network. IFC also mobilised up to €72 million in co-financing (B-loans) for a total package exceeding €120 million. The investment supports 4G network rollout, mobile data capacity expansion, and mobile money infrastructure improvements in Togo and is the largest private telecoms financing in the country. IATI records $59.51M reflecting the combined A+B portion reported by IFC.
